executive_summary.executive_brief: The sole signal change today is an UNFIRE on t2_hyperscaler_capex_revenue [→§3]: Layer 2 returned a 'Reversed' verdict on Q1 2026 actuals, with all four hyperscalers' capex/revenue ratios below the 40% reversal threshold (MSFT 37.2%, GOOGL 32.5%, META 33.7%, AMZN 24.3%), demoting the indicator from Fired to Reversed and shifting the distribution per Rule B — bear probability trims 4pp to 34%, bull extends 3pp to 19%, and base case peak extends one month to 4 months out with return_to_peak_pct restoring to 13% [→§4]. The dominant macro story today is the Samsung strike cluster resolution: the planned 48,000-worker 18-day strike that was the prior brief's leading supply-tightening narrative was called off via a last-minute wage deal reached before the May 21 launch, with multiple sources from WSJ (21:10 UTC May 20) through AI Magazine (10:25 UTC May 21) confirming the suspension — the operative state is strike averted, removing the near-term HBM and DRAM supply tightening risk that was previously priced in and eliminating the anti-trigger for t3_supplier_inventory_rebuild [→§3]; separately, Mirae Asset Securities raised Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) target to KRW 480,000 from KRW 400,000 (+20%) citing accelerating QoQ contract price increases and LPDDR5X +81% / LPDDR4X +72% QoQ in Q2 2026, constituting a strong directional anti-trigger for t3_contract_decline [→§4]. On the big-mover front, SK Hynix surged +11.17% [→§1] — the largest single-session move in the coverage universe today — while Samsung +8.51% and AMD +8.10% also posted outsized gains; Cerebras (CBRS) was the sole decliner at -4.26%, diverging sharply from the broad semi tape on no fundamental catalyst, consistent with late-cycle rotation away from speculative AI-adjacent names [→§1]. The macro backdrop is unambiguously bullish in the near term: NVIDIA reported $81.6B Q1 revenue with "demand gone parabolic" commentary, cited analyst estimates of $1 trillion in hyperscaler capex by 2027 [→§5], Anthropic disclosed $10.9B Q2 revenue and a $1.25B/month SpaceX compute commitment, and CXMT's Shanghai Stock Exchange IPO review next week accelerates the medium-term China DRAM supply narrative that remains the most credible path to cycle turn in H2 2026–H1 2027 [→§4].
